title: Vendor Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) Guidance & Template
content:
Purpose:
This guidance and template are intended to standardize how Redwood Inference evaluates privacy risks associated with third-party vendors, service providers, and partners that process customer or company data. Use this document during vendor onboarding, periodic reviews, and whenever a vendor’s processing changes materially.

Scope:
Applies to all vendors that: 
- Receive any data classified as Customer Data, Personal Data, or Sensitive Personal Data;
- Connect to Redwood production networks or systems; or
- Perform analytics, training, or storage of model-related datasets.

How to use this file:
1) Complete the vendor identification section and data-flow diagram.
2) Populate the data inventory and legal basis fields with vendor-provided artifacts (DPA, SCCs, contract clauses).
3) Walk through the risk checklist and record residual risk + mitigations.
4) Attach evidence in the evidence table and link to the contract and audit reports.
5) Obtain required approvals and enter review cadence.

SECTION A — Vendor Identification
- Vendor legal name: [Vendor Name]
- Vendor primary contact: [Name, email, phone]
- Contract owner / Redwood sponsor: [Product / Eng / CS contact]
- Vendor service description: [Free-text summary of service and business purpose]
- Onboarding type: [Production / Non-production / Pilot]

SECTION B — Data Inventory & Purpose
For each data category the vendor will access, list: category, examples, classification (Customer Data / Personal Data / Sensitive), retention period, and transfer locations.
- Data category 1: e.g., User messages (Customer Data) — examples: chat transcripts, prompt history — retention: 180 days — regions: us-west1, eu-west1
- Data category 2: e.g., Account metadata (Personal Data) — examples: name, email — retention: contract-term + 1 year — regions: us-east4
- Data category 3: e.g., Model weights / artifacts (Proprietary) — handling notes: encryption at rest, access restricted to SREs

SECTION C — Data Flows (high level)
Provide a short narrative plus a small ASCII-style flow map or attach vendor diagram. Indicate ingress points, processing, storage, and egress. Note any cross-border transfers and subprocessors.
Example flow: Customer -> Redwood API -> Vendor preprocessing -> Vendor model inference (transient) -> Redwood returns output -> Vendor logs scrubbed -> Vendor long-term storage (if applicable)

SECTION D — Legal & Contractual Controls
- Contract / DPA status: [Not signed / Draft / Executed] — attach contract id: [contract-xxxx]
- Data processing roles: [Processor / Sub-processor / Joint controller]
- Standard contractual clauses: [Yes / No] — type: [SCCs / EU Addendum / Other]
- Local law exceptions / data residency issues: [notes]
- Insurance: cyber liability coverage amount and policy number if provided

SECTION E — Technical & Organizational Measures (vendor attestation + evidence)
For each control, indicate Attestation (Y/N/Partial), Evidence location (URL or doc id), and Redwood verification notes.
- Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3): [Y/N] — evidence: [link] — notes:
- Encryption at rest (FIPS or AES-256): [Y/N] — evidence: [link] — notes: 
- Key management (vendor-managed / customer-managed / HSM): [description] 
- Access control (RBAC, least privilege): [Y/N] — MFA enforced for admin access? [Y/N] 
- Logging & monitoring: [Y/N] — retention period for logs: [days] 
- Data minimization & deletion procedures: [Y/N] — describe deletion API or process 
- Penetration testing and vulnerability management cadence: [quarterly/annual] — latest report date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Subprocessor disclosure & approval process: [describe] 

SECTION F — Privacy Risk Assessment (scoring matrix)
Use the quick scoring rubric below to highlight high-risk areas requiring contractual or technical mitigation. Provide rationale for each score.
- Likelihood: 1 (Rare) – 5 (Almost certain)
- Impact: 1 (Negligible) – 5 (Severe)
- Risk score = Likelihood x Impact (1–25).

Common risk vectors to evaluate:
1) Persistent storage of raw customer content without redaction
2) Unlimited subprocessor delegation with no notification
3) Cross-border transfers without adequate safeguards
4) Inadequate access controls for production systems
5) Lack of deletion or export mechanisms on termination

Record a row per vector: 
- Vector: "Persistent storage of raw customer content" — Likelihood: [3] — Impact: [5] — Score: [15] — Mitigation: [Contract clause + technical retention policy + audit evidence]

SECTION G — Required Mitigations & Contract Language (boilerplate snippets)
Include recommended clauses the legal team should use. Example clauses below are suggested starting points — legal to finalize.
1) Data minimization & retention: "Vendor shall only store Customer Data for the minimum period necessary to provide the Services and shall delete or anonymize Customer Data upon Customer request or at contract termination, within [X] days."
2) Subprocessor restrictions: "Vendor shall not engage subprocessors without prior written notification; for Tier-1 subprocessors Vendor shall obtain Customer approval where subprocessors will process Sensitive Personal Data."
3) Inspection & audit rights: "Customer shall have the right to conduct, or appoint an independent auditor to conduct, audits of Vendor’s security controls upon agreed notice and under NDA."
4) Data breach obligations: "Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and provide root cause, affected datasets, mitigation steps, and timeline for remediation. Notification timeline: initial report within 48 hours of Vendor awareness."
5) Forensics & evidence preservation: "Vendor shall preserve logs and forensic evidence for a minimum of [90] days or longer if required by investigation; preserve chain-of-custody."

SECTION H — Evidence Log (table rows in text)
- Evidence item 1: SOC2 report (Type II) — Period: [YYYY-YYYY] — Location: [link] — Verified by: [name, date]
- Evidence item 2: Pen-test executive summary — Date: [YYYY-MM-DD] — Location: [link]
- Evidence item 3: DPA signed — Date: [YYYY-MM-DD] — Contract id: [contract-xxxx]

SECTION I — Approval, Residual Risk & Remediation Plan
- Initial reviewer (Security): [name, date]
- Product/owner acceptance: [name, date]
- Legal approval: [name, date]
- Executive sign-off (if needed): [name, date]
- Residual risk category: [Acceptable / Accept with mitigations / High — do not onboard]
- Remediation owner: [name] — Target remediation date: [YYYY-MM-DD] — Status: [open/in-progress/closed]

SECTION J — Review Cadence & Triggers
Standard re-review cadence: 12 months. Re-review triggers: material change to processing, new subprocessors, security incidents, contract renewal.

Appendix A — Quick checklist for onboarding sequence
- Receive vendor security questionnaire and DPA draft
- Confirm data categories and flows
- Request SOC2 or equivalent and pen-test reports
- Confirm encryption and access controls
- Negotiate contractual mitigations (retention, subprocessors, breach timelines)
- Schedule initial technical integration review with Eng/SRE
- Execute DPA & contract; record in contract repository
- Kick off 90-day operational onboarding and monitoring

Appendix B — Example questions to ask vendors (short list)
- Do you persist customer content beyond transient inference? If so, for how long and where?
- Where are your data centers and what regions do you use? Do you rely on public cloud providers?
- Do you use any subprocessors for storage, monitoring, or model training? Provide list and contract status.
- How do you handle deletion requests and data exports? Provide API references if available.
- Provide an outline of your key rotation, HSM usage, and compromise remediation steps.

Notes and guidance for reviewers (working tips)
- If vendor claims no logging, ask for technical proof (e.g., architecture diagram showing ephemeral in-memory only flows or mock mem usage).
- Pay attention to default retention settings; some SaaS defaults keep data for 2+ years unless changed.
- When vendor provides a generic pen-test, request scope to confirm production environment coverage and timing.
- Risk scoring is intentionally conservative for vendors that process Customer Data: prefer contractual controls + technical enforcement.

Template history and next steps
- Created: Jordan Li, initial draft 2025-11-17
- Internal review notes: Marisol Vega (2025-12-02) requested stronger deletion SLAs for model-inference vendors
- Next: circulate to Legal for clause standardization and to Product onboarding team for integration checklist alignment

Placeholders for attachments (attach scanned or linked documents in the contract repository):
- [Link to DPA draft]
- [Link to SOC2 report]
- [Link to pen-test summary]
- [Link to architecture diagram]

End of template.

Revision log (short):
- v0.1 (2025-11-17) Jordan Li — initial template
- v0.2 (2025-12-03) Marisol Vega — added deletion SLA language and evidence log table
- v0.3 (2026-03-10) Security team — updated breach notification timeline to 48 hours and added forensic preservation clause
